claims.text: The initial alloy is a non-equilibrium, supersaturated solid solution containing dispersed metastable phases or intermetallic precursors.
The initial alloy has a density below 6 g/cm3.
Thermal exposure promotes diffusion-driven segregation and nucleation of nano- to micron-scale Mg-rich intermetallic compounds.
Mg-containing compositionally complex alloys can contain intermetallic compounds and predominantly Mg-rich phases.
Intermetallic precipitation partitions Mg from the matrix and enriches interfaces and grain boundaries.
Intermetallic phases and their spatial distribution can affect corrosion by acting either as barriers or as micro-galvanic sites.
Microstructural partitioning caused by Mg-rich precipitates modifies surface chemistry and favors a more protective passivation film.
A TiO2-rich surface film can enhance passivation and lower corrosion current density in a Mg-Ti-Zn alloy.
Differences in atomic size, mixing enthalpy, and diffusivity drive phase separation upon thermal activation.
The evolved microstructure reduces local anodic area and thereby improves corrosion resistance.
The evolved microstructure minimizes defect density at the oxide-scale/substrate interface.
Aged samples will have a more positive corrosion potential than as-cast samples.
Aged samples will have a lower corrosion current density than as-cast samples.
Aged samples will exhibit lower high-temperature oxidation mass gain than as-cast samples.
Aged samples will exhibit less oxide-scale spallation and a more adherent scale than as-cast samples.
Microscopy and diffraction will reveal distinct Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates after aging that are absent from the as-cast microstructure.
The proposed evolution requires enough thermal exposure for diffusion while remaining below incipient melting.
The effect may disappear when alloy composition or processing prevents sufficient diffusion and phase segregation.
The kinetics and quantitative corrosion and oxidation effects depend on the alloying constituents and processing parameters.
